diag.title: GPU Diagnostics
diag.noGpu: Kekenik VFX could not start WebGPU on this device. Nothing is blocked: you can retry, try the software renderer, or continue in limited mode.
diag.iframe: The app runs inside a frame. Open it in its own browser tab: WebGPU is often disabled in iframes.
diag.insecure: The page is not a secure context (use https:// or localhost).
diag.hint.hw: Enable hardware acceleration in the browser settings (System → “Use graphics acceleration when available”) and restart the browser.
diag.hint.chromeGpu: Open chrome://gpu and check that “WebGPU” says “Hardware accelerated”. If it is disabled, update the graphics driver.
diag.hint.flags: Try chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu (Enabled) and, on old GPUs, chrome://flags/#ignore-gpu-blocklist; then relaunch.
diag.hint.vulkan: Linux: also enable chrome://flags/#enable-vulkan and install Vulkan drivers (mesa-vulkan-drivers).
diag.hint.firefox: Firefox: open about:config and set dom.webgpu.enabled to true (a recent Firefox release is required).
diag.hint.safari: Safari 18 or newer (macOS 15 / iOS 18) is required. Older versions: Develop → Feature Flags → WebGPU.
diag.hint.driver: Update the graphics driver. Remote desktop sessions and virtual machines often expose no GPU: use “Try software renderer”.
